title: Review: Capacitance and capacitor energy; Capacitor charging and discharging; Graphs and data analysis; Magnetic flux and Faraday's/Lenz's laws
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; EL09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; EL10-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL09-1#N.2, EL10-1#N.4b, MG06-1#N.9b, MS03-1#N.15, EL09-1#N.5, EL10-1#N.8, MG06-1#N.14, MG06-1#N.3c. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Farad
items.clue: Unit equal to 1 C V⁻¹; real values are usually given in μF, nF or pF.

items.label: Electric potential energy
items.clue: What is stored by the work of separating +Q from the opposite charge.

items.label: Time constant
items.clue: Found as –1/gradient of a graph of ln V against t; 5.0 s in the example.

items.label: Magnetic flux
items.clue: How much field passes through an area: think of the number of lines through it.

questions.stem: Predict first. An uncharged parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a battery and left until it is fully charged. Which statement correctly describes how the capacitor becomes charged?

options.text: Electrons move from one plate, through the wires and battery, to the other plate.
Electrons cross the gap between the two plates, from one plate to the other.
The battery creates new charge and places some on each of the two plates.
The battery adds charge to one plate, and the other plate remains neutral.

questions.stem: A capacitor is charged through a resistor by a battery. At time t₁ the p.d. across the capacitor is one quarter of the battery's emf. At a later time t₂ it is three quarters of the emf. What is the current at t₂ divided by the current at t₁?
questions.explanation: Current = (p.d. across the resistor) ÷ R. At t₁ that p.d. is ¾ of the emf; at t₂ it is ¼. Ratio: ¼ ÷ ¾ = 1/3.

questions.stem: The south pole of a bar magnet is pulled away from one end of a coil whose ends are joined. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The near end of the coil becomes a south pole, pushing the magnet away faster.
The near end becomes a north pole, so work must be done to pull the magnet away.
No current flows, because the magnet is moving away from the coil, not towards it.
The near end becomes a north pole, and the energy for the current comes from the magnet's magnetism.

questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change. A north pole attracts the retreating south pole, so you do work, and that work becomes electrical energy.

questions.stem: A best-fit line has gradient 2.50. The steepest line through all the error bars has gradient 2.65 (same units). What is the percentage uncertainty in the gradient?
A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to an ideal 12 V battery. When the capacitor is fully charged, its positive plate carries a charge of 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ C. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?

An uncharged capacitor is charged through a 3.0 kΩ resistor by an ideal battery of emf 9.0 V, all connected in series. What is the current in the resistor at the instant when the potential difference across the capacitor is 6.0 V?

options.text: 3.0 mA
2.0 mA
5.0 mA

questions.stem: A thick aluminium plate swings as a pendulum through the gap between the poles of a strong magnet, and stops after a few swings. An identical plate with many deep slots cut into it swings for much longer. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Aluminium is attracted by magnets, and the solid plate has more metal for the magnet to grip.
Currents induced in the moving solid plate oppose its motion; the slots block their paths.
The slots let air pass through the plate, so the slotted plate meets far less air resistance.
The induced currents draw energy from the magnet, which grows weaker during each swing of the solid plate.

questions.stem: A flat coil of 150 turns, each of area 20 cm², is placed with its plane at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.40 T. What is the flux linkage of the coil?

options.text: 1.2 Wb
